sentences.text: I have heard Sri. S. Rajeev, Sri. Renjith B. Marar, Sri. Sarath Babu Kottakkal, the learned counsel for the applicants, Sri. M.C. Ashi and K.A. Noushad, the learned Senior Public Prosecutors.
Perused the case diary.
5. The learned counsel for the applicants submitted that the applicants are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the present case.

The learned Senior Public Prosecutors, on the other hand, submitted that the alleged incident occurred as part of the applicants' intentional criminal acts, and if they are released on bail at this stage, it will affect the course of the investigation.
6.
The law regarding the grant or refusal of pre- arrest bail is well settled.
Pre-arrest bail cannot be granted as a matter of course.
The power under Section 482 of BNSS could be exercised only when a special case is made out, that too, recording reasons thereof.
Perusal of the case diary reveals that the accusation made against the applicants is very serious in nature, and it prima facie shows a premeditated criminal act on their part.
The accused No.1 is the President and the remaining accused are the Board Members of the Society while some of the loans were sanctioned.
The applicants were present in the Board Meeting when the loans were sanctioned.

Considering the gravity of the offence and stage of the investigation, I am of the view that these are not a fit cases where the extraordinary jurisdiction vested with this Court under Section 482 of BNSS could be invoked.
However, since the accused No.9/applicant No.4 in B.A.No.702/2026 is a cancer survivor lady aged 60 years, she can be granted pre-arrest bail.

The learned counsel for the applicants submitted that the B.A.Nos. 527, 582 & 702 of 2026 2026:KER:29495 accused Nos. 1, 5, 3, 4, 7, 8,
10 and 12 are ready to surrender before the investigating officer.

Accordingly, these bail applications are disposed of as follows:
(i) The accused No.9 shall be released on bail in the event of her arrest on executing a bond for Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with two solvent sureties for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the arresting officer/investigating officer, as the case may be.
( ii) The accused No.9 shall fully cooperate with the investigation, including subjecting herself to the deemed police custody for discovery, if any, as and when demanded.
(iii) The accused No.9 shall appear before the investigating officer between 10.00 a.m. and 11.00 a.m. every Saturday until further orders.
She shall also appear before the investigating officer as and when required.
(iv) The accused No.9 shall not commit any offence of a like nature while on bail.
